To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-1 time series for MowEvents detection can be improved by using a deep learning approach for the reconstruction of dense NDVI time series.
the use of Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-1 data for the detection of Mowing Event in permanent grasslands is challenging due to the heterogeneity of the environment and the complexity of the task.

the use of Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-1 data, together with the proposed deep learning-based strategy, can be used to obtain dense and homogeneous NDVI time series, which can be exploited for MowEves detection.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: (i) the development of innovative and efficient methods for the extraction of biophysical information from satellite images; (ii) the development and implementation of methods and tools to support the decision-making process in the field of environmental monitoring; (iii) the analysis of the impact of climate change and land use changes on the environment.
the detection of mowing events, which is a key step to monitor and assess the status of grasslands, and to understand their dynamics and evolution.
the detection of MowEve in PG using S2 and S1 time series and deep learning approaches, with the aim of providing a complete and robust detection of the MowEve.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed methodology is promising for the detection of MowEve, but further research is required to fully exploit the potential of the proposed approach.
the proposed methodology is able to reconstruct dense NDVIs series, but it is still necessary to improve the detection of MowEve.
the proposed methodology can detect MowEve with a high accuracy (AUC > 0.95) and a high completeness (> 90%).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the integration of optical and SAR data is a promising strategy to detect and monitor MowEve in grasslands.
a) the integration of S1 and S2 data allows to improve MowEve identification and b) a deep-learning-based approach is a promising tool for MowEves detection.

i) the proposed deep-based approach for S2 and S1 data fusion is able to reconstruct dense NDVIs time series with a high accuracy, ii) the proposed deep-learning-based MowEve detector is able to detect MowEve with a high accuracy and iii) the proposed MowEve detectors outperform state-of-the-art methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a robust and complete MowEve monitoring requires the exploitation of both optical and Synthetic Appear Radar data.
S1 data is a powerful and complementary tool for detecting MowEve in the context of PG monitoring.
S1 time series are not able to capture the MowEve signal, while S2 data are able to detect MowEve with high accuracy.
